beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: infrastructure creation and operating a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant.
Infrastructure projects include railway platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion and track laying, various types of bridges, and bituminous and concrete roads.

Contracts are won through a competitive tender process: the client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, bidders submit quotes, and the lowest bidder is awarded the job. The contractor must then deposit a performance guarantee.

Major clients include Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd (MRVCL), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), and Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA). Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the orders on hand.
Revenue is highly concentrated: key customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018.
The company's operations are focused on Mumbai and Maharashtra, with a 'strong order book' according to the filing, though the absolute order book value is not disclosed.
The RMC plant is a state-of-the-art facility at Kashimira, Thane, producing ready-mix concrete for construction projects.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined steadily from ₹90.21 crore in fiscal 2015 to ₹60.53 crore in fiscal 2018, a drop of about 33%.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹0.96 crore in FY2014, ₹0.78 crore in FY2015, ₹0.33 crore in FY2016, ₹0.16 crore in FY2017, and then a sharp jump to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) ranged from ₹6.76 crore (FY2017) to ₹9.46 crore (FY2015), and was ₹9.29 crore in FY2018.

Short-term borrowings increased from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014 to ₹35.37 crore in FY2018. Long-term borrowings were ₹5.87 crore in FY2014, rose to ₹6.73 crore in FY2015, then fell sharply to ₹1.33 crore by FY2018.

The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, a risk noted in the filing. Specific cash flow figures are not extracted, but the risk disclosure states that sustained negative cash flow could adversely impact the business.
Total assets grew from ₹70.62 crore in FY2014 to ₹82.32 crore in FY2018.

beats.beat: Mr. Amit Bholanath Mishra is the sole promoter, holding 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issue share capital.

The board of directors includes Amit Bholanath Mishra (Managing Director), Bharat Kumar Parmar (Whole Time Director), Shree Prakash Singh (Whole Time Director), and Mukesh Pandey (Whole Time Director). Each of the three non-promoter directors holds only 300 equity shares.
Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (Chief Financial Officer, a Chartered Accountant aged 28) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, ACS aged 26).

Related-party transactions for fiscal 2018 include loan taken from KMP/Board of Directors ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties ₹324.3 lakhs as on March 31, 2018.

Governance flags: Two companies promoted by the promoter (Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited) were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation. The company has issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price. No monitoring agency has been appointed for fund deployment.
No criminal cases have been filed against directors, and none are on the RBI list of willful defaulters.

beats.beat: Construction and infrastructure contribute about 8% to India's GDP and are highly fragmented and working-capital intensive.

Demand is driven by government flagship programs such as 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, and Power for All, as well as eased FDI norms in 15 sectors including real estate and construction development.
The logistics sector, a key part of infrastructure, is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020.
The company faces competition from both organized and unorganized players in a market that is 'highly fragmented'.
Headwinds identified in the filing include a slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches affecting profitability, and changes in government policies.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor that also operates a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant. It builds railway platforms, bridges, roads, and structures for government clients like Indian Railways and the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai.
The company is raising up to ₹44.28 crore (at face value) through a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares, with no offer for sale — all proceeds go to the company.
The primary object of the issue is to meet working capital requirements; the company has seen revenue decline in recent years and carries significant debt.

beats.beat: The issue consists of a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, at a price to be determined. There is no offer for sale — all shares are new.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited, and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
The net proceeds will be used for two purposes: (1) meeting working capital requirements of ₹1,130 lakhs (₹11.30 crore), and (2) general corporate purposes, whose allocation is not disclosed.

beats.beat: Heavy dependence on Indian Railways: Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book, and the top customers accounted for 57% of revenue. Losing this client would drastically reduce revenue.
Revenue depends on winning bids: the company relies on government tenders awarded to the lowest bidder. Failure to win bids or negotiating lower values could materially affect performance.
Negative cash flows: the company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, which could strain operations and lead to default on obligations.
Geographical concentration: a major portion of revenue comes from Mumbai and surrounding regions. Any adverse local developments could disproportionately hurt the company.
Unsecured loans repayable on demand: as of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans that can be called in at any time, posing a liquidity risk.

beats.beat: For fiscal 2018, the company's basic earnings per share (EPS) was ₹12.59, and diluted EPS was ₹3.82. Return on net worth (RoNW) was 28.14%, and net asset value (NAV) per share was ₹44.71.

The DRHP includes a comparison of accounting ratios with peer group companies, but the peer names and their financials are not disclosed in the extracted facts. Therefore, we cannot compute an implied price range or build a peer comparison table.
The issue price will be determined by the company in consultation with the lead manager and will be justified by reference to these accounting ratios, according to the filing.
